correctness.rationale: For any set containing reflections, choosing one reflection as a base expresses the translation subgroup generated by the set as the vector-space span of the translations and all differences between reflection parameters. This gives both necessity and sufficiency for generation, proves d(G)=t+1, and reduces pair extension to elementary rank counts. The three pair cases yield the stated adjacency relation and exact degrees. The divisibility follows from the element orders p and 2. The packaged replay reconstructs the group law and minimum generating graphs for two full rank-two cases and checks every predicted rank-three edge by direct subgroup closure.

The theorem settles it on a natural infinite nonnilpotent family whose minimum generator number is unbounded, so it advances the genuinely higher-rank regime rather than the already known 2-generated case.
